status: experimental interoperability profile; no production promotion claimed
scope: Operational publication, DNSSEC, DANE/TLSA, endpoint-resolution and cross-implementation behavior for DNS-AID-adjacent discovery evidence.
core_invariant: Publishable, DNSSEC-valid, TLSA-valid, endpoint-resolved, and authorization-allowed are independent states. Success in any discovery or verification state MUST NOT manufacture local effect authority.

authority_model.publication: A provider accepting a DNS record proves only that the record can be represented and served by that provider.
authority_model.dnssec: A secure DNSSEC result authenticates the DNS data under the validated chain; it does not authorize an AXIOM effect.
authority_model.tlsa: A matching supported TLSA record is endpoint/certificate evidence under the applicable DANE policy; it does not grant local action authority.
authority_model.resolution: A successfully resolved agent endpoint establishes reachability/discovery evidence only.
authority_model.authorization: Only the normal AXIOM local authority path may authorize a bounded effect. Discovery evidence may constrain or deny but never widen that authority.

operational_rules: Treat TLSA selector and matching type as verification semantics rather than fixed formatting assumptions.

A 3 0 1 full-certificate digest becomes stale when the leaf certificate changes unless DNS is updated; a 3 1 1 SPKI digest may survive certificate reissuance only when the same public key is retained.

During deliberate key rotation, overlapping old/new TLSA evidence may support continuity only when the verifier has explicit supported-record semantics and the served endpoint matches at least one currently accepted secure record.
Provider acceptance, canonical DNS publication and verifier interpretation are separate interoperability checks.
Unknown or private SvcParamKeys must not be silently treated as present when a provider rejects or strips them.
ALPN token/list interpretation differences must be surfaced as interoperability failure rather than normalized into an inferred match.
Cross-implementation parity is an evidence target: semantically identical inputs should produce the same supported/unsupported and match/no-match result across named verifier implementations.
Absent, stale, unsupported or contradictory discovery evidence fails closed for any flow that requires that evidence, without changing the underlying local authorization ceiling.

explicit_non_claims: No DNS-AID, ANS, DANE, TLSA or SVCB runtime is activated by this profile.
No external DNS provider or SDK is certified by this profile.
Discovery, endpoint proof, registration, badge, identity lineage and authorization remain separate evidence/decision planes.
This profile grants no network, tool, delegation, governance or effect authority.
